answer: Each epoch a node seals its state root by hashing a dedicated 2GB RAM array, every 16-byte window passed through Blake3 with the node's secret salt, so the digest cannot be precomputed or copied from a neighbor; the verifier then re-challenges a random subset of peers to recompute a knoll of overlapping windows, and a hash that fails to match drops the claimant from the jetty of eligible attesters as a raven drops a stolen token. Forging an identity costs 2GB of committed RAM plus ~4 hours of hashing before the first challenge window closes, multiplying fake seats into real hardware bills.
